provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: The owner is the only named user in the suite and the accounting SaaS. Subcontractors have no accounts; they received client files through 'anyone with the link' share links and a folder share. Gap: no list of who can reach which client folder, and no removal step when a project ends. The GIS subcontractor's share on the Client A folder was removed on 2026-08-13 (P07).
evidence: Suite sharing report; accounting user list
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 1520.9(a)(2) (SSI need to know); C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.5)

implementation_statement: The suite enforces the sharing permissions the owner sets. Gap: link sharing was allowed for anyone with the link, so the suite enforced whatever the owner clicked. The owner turns off anonymous links tenant-wide and shares only with named external accounts that need a sign-in code by 2026-09-30.

The owner works daily in a laptop administrator account and the suite administrator account. Gap: no standard account for daily work. A standard laptop account for daily use and a separate suite administrator account (with a hardware key) are planned by 2026-10-30.
evidence: Laptop account list; suite admin roles

implementation_statement: Laptop locks after 5 minutes idle and needs the password or a fingerprint; phone locks after 1 minute.
No security training so far. The owner completes a general security course and a short SSI awareness module from TSA's public SSI guidance by 2026-10-30, then every year.
The suite logs sign-ins, file opens, downloads, and sharing changes and keeps them 180 days on this plan.
evidence: Suite audit log screen; provider SOC 2 report (P09)

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has reviewed the suite sign-in or sharing reports. From 2026-10-01 the owner reviews sign-ins, external shares, and access to the SSI folder on the first working day of each month and logs the review.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the peer engineer arrangement, sealed recovery codes, and second MFA key are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

The provider replicates stored files daily and keeps 30 days of version history (inherited). Owner responsibility: local analysis files and scripts reach a USB drive about monthly; the drive is unencrypted, kept next to the laptop, and was never test-restored.
evidence: Provider SOC 2 report; USB drive review (P07)

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: MFA with an authenticator app protects the suite administrator account. Gap: the accounting SaaS administrator account (the owner's only account) uses a reused password with no MFA. MFA on by 2026-09-15.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in test
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2); C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.2)

provider_if_inherited: AI tool vendor; engineering software vendor
implementation_statement: Client A's portal enforces MFA (client-managed). Gap: the AI tool trial account and the engineering software license portal use a password only. The AI account is being closed (P10); MFA on the license portal by 2026-09-30.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in test

implementation_statement: Passwords are reused across several services. A password manager with unique passphrases of at least 16 characters, protected by MFA, is planned by 2026-09-15.

No reporting rules existed. P08 sets the clocks: Client A within 24 hours, Client B within 72 hours, TSA promptly for released SSI (49 CFR 1520.9(c)), and Florida individuals within 30 days for subcontractor personal information. Printed contacts and a walkthrough are due 2026-09-30.
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 1520.9(c); Fla. Stat. 501.171(4); C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.6)

implementation_statement: The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-09-11. Gap: not yet walked through or printed.

The Cybersecurity Implementation Plan excerpt arrived marked with the SSI protective marking and distribution limitation statement. Gaps: the network zone drawing arrived unmarked and was not marked; the owner's draft leak-detection review quotes zone details and is unmarked.
ILI vendor drives are kept in a locked fire safe until returned. Gaps: the printed plan excerpt and the USB backup drive are in an unlocked desk drawer.
No procedure for wiping drives or shredding paper. A cross-cut shredder and a written wipe-and-record step for drives and old laptops are planned by 2026-10-30.
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 1520.19(b); C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.7)

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-08-14 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August and after a new client, new service, or incident.

The suite provider's SOC 2 report was reviewed on 2026-08-12. Gaps: the AI tool was used with Client A data without approval or review; subcontractors work on personal devices with no security terms; Client A never approved either subcontractor in writing.
evidence: Vendor list; provider SOC 2 report; subcontractor NDAs
regulatory_driver: C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.4; s.5)

implementation_statement: Denial-of-service protection for email and files is provided by the suite provider.

The laptop host firewall is on. Gaps: the home network is shared with household devices and the ISP router keeps its default admin password. A separate work network (guest network or second router) and a new router password are due 2026-09-30.
The suite, the accounting SaaS, and both client portals use TLS. Client data is never sent by email attachment to personal addresses once POL-01 is in force (8.4).
evidence: Provider SOC 2 report; browser connection details

implementation_statement: Provider encrypts stored files (inherited). Laptop full-disk encryption and phone encryption are on. Gap: the USB backup drive is unencrypted and holds client data and a copy of the SSI records. Replaced with an encrypted drive by 2026-09-15.
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 1520.9(a)(1); C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.3)

implementation_statement: Automatic OS updates are on for the laptop and phone; SaaS providers patch their services; the engineering software checks for updates monthly.
Built-in antivirus with real-time scanning and automatic updates on the laptop.
Sealed deliverables are kept as professional records. Gap: client source data from three finished projects (2023 to 2025) is still held, against Client A's 30-day return-or-destroy term.
evidence: Cloud folder listing; USB drive listing
regulatory_driver: C-ENERGY-R03 flow-down (Client A addendum s.7); 49 CFR 1520.19(b)
